inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 June 2026: 4,611.7m ordinary shares in issue less 185.9m treasury shares = 4,425.8m outstanding, plus ~78m employee share-scheme dilution (H1-2026 diluted 4,786m less basic 4,512m less 196m convertible conversion). The 2028 convertible was redeemed in May 2026 (EUR 3m notional remains) so no convertible dilution is carried. Count held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The remaining ~EUR 700m of the EUR 1.5bn excess-cash return (to Feb 2027) is value-neutral under the house method and is not netted from the count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report, share-based payment charge EUR 58m (IAG.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:12346); no net-share-settlement tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0), so the cash-flow add-back is the combined figure
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 acquisition of treasury shares EUR 1,243m (CSV ShareRepurchases); H1-2026 a further EUR 667m. The flat count is funded: IAG is an active repurchaser (c. EUR 800m of the EUR 1.5bn Feb-2026 programme completed by Aug 2026).
inputs.fx_note: EUR -> GBp: EURGBP=X 0.8461 (Yahoo Finance, 2026-10-09T22:18Z) x 100 = 84.61 pence per euro. Parity check against the Madrid dual listing: IAG.MC EUR 4.921 (close 2026-10-09T15:35Z) x 0.8461 = 416.4p vs the observed IAG.L close of 415.9p, a 0.1% tie confirming rate, direction and pence basis. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate; re-derive the rate when the price is refreshed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in EUR, the currency of the flows. 10y Bund ~2.7% + airline equity beta ~1.4 x ERP 5.5% = cost of equity ~10.4%; cost of debt ~4.3% pre-tax (May-2026 2031/2034 senior bonds) / ~3.2% after tax; weights ~76% equity (EUR 22bn market cap) / 24% ex-lease gross debt (EUR 7.0bn) give ~8.7%, rounded to 9.0%. The same 9.0% is used in every scenario: cyclicality, fuel and geopolitical risk are charged in the flows via the scenario paths and weights, not a second time in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full IFRS-16 lease payment (FY2025: principal EUR 1,344m in financing + interest EUR 406m in operating = EUR 1,750m, 5.3% of revenue; H1-2026: 722 + 175 = EUR 897m, ~5.6%) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities (EUR 6,907m at 30 Jun 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A used for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 total D&A 2,628 less ROU depreciation 1,113 = EUR 1,515m, 4.6% of revenue) so the lease is charged once. Asset-financed liabilities (EUR 5,217m, secured aircraft financing classified as borrowings) remain in net debt because their interest is a financing cost, not a lease. Lease cost is glided down (5.4% -> 4.5%) as IAG shifts fleet financing from leases to owned/asset-financed aircraft (new leases EUR 543m FY2025 vs EUR 1,315m FY2023), with capex held at ~10% of revenue so total fleet cash cost stays ~15% of revenue, in line with FY2024-25 (15.6-15.7%).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is EUR 6m; immaterial, no adjustment.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 (H1-2026 note 11): bank and other loans 1,739 + convertible bonds 4 + asset-financed liabilities 5,217 = EUR 6,960m ex-lease borrowings, less cash, cash equivalents and current interest-bearing deposits EUR 9,175m = net CASH EUR 2,215m. Cross-check: adding lease liabilities 6,907 gives IAG's own reported net debt of EUR 4,692m. Because the cash pile sits in the bridge, FY2025 finance income of EUR 279m is stripped from the FCF base (net cash ex-lease > 1x the owner-FCF base). Excluded from the bridge: the EUR 2,060m employee-benefit (pension) asset, which is an IFRIC-14-restricted accounting surplus on the BA schemes and not distributable cash; and EUR 298m of other equity investments (immaterial, income not stripped).
inputs.fcf_note: reported_fcf is on the lease-consistent basis: IAG's headline FY2025 free cash flow of EUR 3,146m (OCF 6,588 less capex 3,442; interest paid incl. lease interest and interest received are inside OCF) less lease principal repayments EUR 1,344m = EUR 1,802m. last_fcf = 1,802 - SBC 58 - interest income 279 = EUR 1,465m. FY2025 OCF carried a one-off EUR 442m HMRC VAT appeal payment, so the underlying figure is ~EUR 1.9bn; the engine builds the forward flows from components and does not scale from last_fcf.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row: operating company, non-US and cyclical, plus owner-fcf-adaptations for currency, leases and risk-once). First valuation of this ticker, no memory entry. FY2025 was a peak-cycle year (operating margin 15.1%, top of the 12-15% target range; RoIC 18.5%), and FY2026 guidance has been cut repeatedly (capacity to flat, fuel cost to EUR 8.3-8.6bn, capex to EUR 3.4bn, FCF below the EUR 3.0bn originally guided) on Middle East route suspensions and fuel. The base case therefore glides the pre-SBC EBITDA margin from ~21.8% in FY2026 (op margin ~13%) to a 21.0% mid-cycle terminal (~12.8% op margin, the middle of management's range), not the 23.2% FY2025 print. Cash tax ramps from the FY2025 actual ~11% of EBIT (EUR 488m; Spanish and UK deferred tax assets of EUR 675m still unwinding) to a 23% blended statutory-like rate over six years. Working-capital capture is 10% of the revenue change (deferred ticket and Avios revenue grew EUR 203m on EUR 1,113m of revenue growth in FY2025). Terminal cap 12x owner FCF for a cyclical; Gordon at 9%/2% would be 14.6x so the cap binds. band_position is reported but the house/street band is narrow (SBC 0.17% of revenue). Note for the sanity check: inputs.total_debt is ex-lease by design (treatment B); the CSV TotalDebt of 13,867 includes lease liabilities.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management medium-term capacity growth (2-3% ASK) plus yield/loyalty mix; cross-checked against the FY2019-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 4.5% which spans the pre-COVID base. The 3yr/5yr CAGRs are COVID-recovery artefacts (FY2020 revenue EUR 7.8bn, FY2021 equity EUR 0.8bn) and are not usable as forward rates.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 55.6% vs revenue 12.9% and EPS 101.6%: all three are distorted by the FY2020-22 COVID trough and recovery; the owner-FCF series (lease-consistent) is negative in FY2019-FY2023 so no FCF CAGR is meaningful. fcf_3yr_cagr is on the pre-lease house basis (869 -> 2,809) and overstates for the same reason.
historical_growth.notes: Reported FCF CAGR vs SBC-adjusted: SBC is 0.17% of revenue, so the adjustment does not change the growth picture; the lease adjustment does, turning FY2019-23 owner FCF negative.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +1% on flat capacity (H1 +1.0%, H2 booked revenue in line with last year) and a ~13% operating margin as ~60% of the ~EUR 1.2bn fuel increase is recovered; capacity growth resumes at 3-3.5% in FY2027-28 as Middle East routes reopen and A321XLR/787/737 deliveries land, then fades to 2%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin settles at 21.0% (op margin ~12.8%, mid-range of the 12-15% target) rather than the 23.2% FY2025 peak: Loyalty growth and transformation savings offset LCC short-haul pressure and higher airport/carbon costs across a cycle. Capex ~10% of revenue (FY2026 guidance EUR 3.4bn) with lease cash gliding from 5.4% to 4.5% as the fleet shifts toward owned/asset-financed aircraft. Cash tax ramps 12% -> 23% as deferred tax assets unwind.

bull.narrative: Middle East airspace reopens and fuel normalises through FY2027, so FY2026 lands at the upper end of guidance and capacity growth runs 4.5-5% in FY2027-29 (Iberia Plan de Vuelo 2030 XLR network, Vueling Project Rumbo, BA premium short-haul). IAG Loyalty reaches its ~EUR 1bn operating-profit target and Aer Lingus's restructuring restores Group-level margins, lifting the sustained pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 23% (op margin ~15%, the top of the range, which FY2025 showed is achievable). Fleet renewal matures so capex eases to 9.5% of revenue. Same WACC and terminal cap as base: the upside is in the flows, not a cheaper discount rate.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance (flat revenue, ~12% op margin) and the cycle turns in FY2027: a consumer/corporate travel downturn coincides with a prolonged Middle East conflict keeping fuel at EUR 8.5bn+, revenue falls 6% and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin drops to 15.5% (op margin ~7%), the kind of year airlines deliver every 8-10 years (FY2009, FY2020). Recovery follows in FY2028-29 but the Group settles at a 19.5% margin (op margin ~11%, below its target range) because LCC short-haul capacity growth, Aer Lingus's restructuring and rising Heathrow, ETS and SAF costs cap pricing power. Fleet deliveries are contractual, so capex cannot be cut in the downturn and lease cash stays elevated. Owner FCF goes negative in the downturn year; the balance sheet (net cash ex-lease, EUR 11.9bn liquidity, 0.6x leverage) absorbs it so this is an earnings bear, not a solvency one.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle airline: FY2026 absorbs the fuel shock at a ~13% operating margin, capacity growth of 3-3.5% resumes in FY2027-28, and the Group settles at an op margin of ~12.8% (pre-SBC EBITDA 21.0%), the middle of its 12-15% range, rather than the 15.1% FY2025 peak. Lease cash glides from 5.4% to 4.5% of revenue as the fleet shifts to owned aircraft while capex holds at ~10%; cash tax ramps 12% -> 23%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fuel and airspace normalise, capacity grows 4.5-5% for three years on Iberia's XLR network and Vueling's 737 plan, Loyalty reaches ~EUR 1bn profit and Aer Lingus is fixed, so the ~15% FY2025 operating margin becomes the sustained level (pre-SBC EBITDA 23%) and capex eases to 9.5% of revenue as fleet renewal matures.
scenario_narratives.bear: Cyclical downturn in FY2027 (revenue -6%, op margin ~7%) on recession plus a prolonged fuel shock, with contractual fleet capex and leases uncuttable; recovery to an ~11% op margin (pre-SBC EBITDA 19.5%), below the target range, as LCC short-haul pressure, Aer Lingus and Heathrow/ETS/SAF costs cap pricing power. Owner FCF is negative in the downturn year but the balance sheet carries it.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: FY2025 was a peak-cycle year, FY2026 guidance has already been cut on capacity, fuel, capex and FCF, management itself flags reduced Q2/Q3 visibility, and airlines reliably deliver a loss-making year once a decade, so a downturn inside a 10-year horizon is closer to likely than remote. Not higher than 30% because net cash ex-lease, EUR 11.9bn liquidity and 0.6x leverage make the bear an earnings case, not a solvency case. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right (fuel/airspace normalisation, Loyalty hitting EUR 1bn, Aer Lingus restructuring succeeding) while short-haul LCC pressure is structural. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: IAG is valued as a cyclical operating company on an owner-FCF basis, with IFRS-16 leases charged as an operating cost (treatment B) and lease liabilities excluded from net debt, which leaves the Group in a EUR 2.2bn net cash position ex-lease. The anchor is a mid-cycle margin, not the record FY2025 print: the base case assumes the business earns the middle of management's 12-15% operating-margin range across the cycle, with a one-in-ten-years downturn given 30% weight. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, at a single 9% EUR WACC. The terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF, appropriate for an airline; the Heathrow slot moat, the AA transatlantic joint business and the capital-light Loyalty business are what justify a cap at the top of the cyclical range rather than below it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Fuel: FY2026 fuel guided at EUR 8.3-8.6bn vs ~EUR 7.0-7.4bn originally, with only ~60% recovered through pricing and cost actions; a sustained jet-fuel spike compresses margins far faster than the base path assumes
Cycle timing: the model assumes FY2025 was the peak; if a downturn arrives earlier or is deeper than the bear's -6% revenue / 15.5% EBITDA margin, the weighted value falls further

Lease-to-owned fleet shift: the model glides lease cash down and holds capex at ~10%; if fleet renewal (A321XLR, 787, 737) pushes combined fleet cash above the ~15% of revenue assumed, owner FCF is overstated
Cash tax normalisation: FY2025 cash tax was ~11% of EBIT on unwinding deferred tax assets; the ramp to 23% is a judgment and a faster unwind cuts value
Short-haul competition and Aer Lingus: structural LCC capacity growth and a failed Aer Lingus restructuring would hold the Group below its 12-15% margin range, which is the bear's terminal state
Currency: flows are EUR, the quote is GBp; a 5% move in EUR/GBP moves the pence value ~5% with no change in the business
